answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can start at a single vertex: every identity must hold a kernel of earned reputation before it can vote or attest. A newcomer joins with zero trust and gains standing only by completing small, independently checkable tasks over time. When a tide of fresh identities arrives, the system throttles their collective weight until each one has a distinct work history. An attacker then faces a real cost: forging a hundred trusted agents means paying for a hundred histories of genuine work, while an honest agent pays that effort only once.
